title: Incident → Eval Artifactization: structured mapping & playbook for config/model regressions
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Background: Recent customer-facing incidents showed we are slow to translate production regressions caused by config or model changes into deterministic evals. Engineers currently reconstruct artifacts manually (prompts, prefixes, traffic traces, model+quantization flags), which delays root-cause verification and reintroduction of golden tests.

This ticket scopes an automated 'incident→eval' artifactization pipeline and a short playbook so every incident that plausibly impacts quality produces a reproducible eval snapshot, a canonical test case, and a traceable link from the incident to the eval run. The goal is to reduce mean time from incident detection to captured regression eval from days to <=4 hours for P0/P1 events and to stop relying on ad-hoc manual reconstructions.

High-level components:
- Incident annotation schema (what metadata to capture: route, model hash, quantization profile, config delta, sample request/response, streaming boundary state).
- Lightweight artifactizer service that pulls relevant logs/traces and outputs a deterministic eval bundle (prompt set, expected outputs, tokenization metadata).
- Integration with existing eval harness to auto-enqueue smoke evals and layout a diff report in the incident ticket.
- Playbook that guides on triage severity -> eval priority mapping and follow-up steps for developers/PMs.

Why this is different: Instead of adding more eval coverage blindly, this system ties eval generation directly to observed production regressions so we create targeted golden tests that reflect real failure modes and protect against reintroduction.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Incident annotation schema published in Confluence and added as a required field on P0/P1 incident templates.
2) Artifactizer prototype can, given an incident ID, assemble a reproducible eval bundle containing: sample requests (<=50), tokenization metadata, model+quantization flags, and a seedable runner config.
3) One production incident (test case TBD) is exercised end-to-end: artifact created, smoke eval run completes, and a regression diff is posted back to the Linear ticket automatically.
4) Automation creates a golden-test PR template (with bundle attached) so PM/Design can approve for regression suite inclusion.
5) Documentation/playbook and a short demo session for on-call and SRE completed.

investigation_summary: Root cause pattern observed across recent incidents: canary/config rollouts occasionally change runtime options (quantization profile or routing policy) without running an automated smoke eval that captures tokenizer/streaming boundaries. On top of that, traces lacked deterministic KV-cache prefix length and streaming sequence ids which made manual reconstruction error-prone. The artifactizer will close the loop by capturing the exact runtime footprint at error time and producing seedable, minimal eval bundles.
